risks.title: Dependence on USA-Mexico passenger traffic
risks.score_rationale: Major risk disclosed at the beginning of Item 1A with highly intensive language (repeated use of « material adverse effect »). 61-62% of Mexico's international traffic originates from the USA; 51-52% of Mexican passenger revenue depends on international passengers. Trend is stable but structural vulnerability to U.S. trade and immigration policies remains high.

risks.title: Political and economic instability Mexico-USA-Colombia
risks.score_rationale: Major geopolitical risk with highly alarming language (« material adverse effect », « cannot assure »). Disclosed early in Item 1A with details on Trump administration changes, USMCA, and reciprocal tariffs. Clear upward trend with new measures expected in 2025-2026. Very high weight for a regional airport operator.

risks.title: Health crises and pandemics affecting air traffic
risks.score_rationale: Systemic risk mentioned multiple times in Item 1A with references to COVID-19, H1N1, and avian flu. Language is moderate but clear on past impact (COVID-19) and future potential. Trend is stable but residual risk remains high post-pandemic. Applicable to all ASRMF airports.

risks.title: Natural disasters (hurricanes, earthquakes)
risks.score_rationale: Operational risk specific to ASRMF's geography (southeast Mexico, Colombia, Puerto Rico). Intensive language with concrete examples (Hurricanes Irma, Maria, Fiona 2022; Puerto Rico earthquakes 2019-2020). Trend is stable but experts note increasing frequency and severity due to climate change. Insurance coverage limited (no business interruption coverage).

risks.title: Internal armed conflicts in Colombia (ELN, FARC)
risks.score_rationale: Regional risk specific to Colombian operations. Moderate language (« cannot predict ») but acknowledges recent escalation in El Catatumbo and past impact on El Caraño airport. Trend is upward (« recently escalated »). Moderate weight as impact is limited to Colombian operations, not core Mexican assets.

risks.title: Prolonged economic crisis in Puerto Rico (PROMESA, PREPA)
risks.score_rationale: Risk specific to LMM Airport (60% ASRMF joint venture). Detailed disclosure on recession since 2006, PROMESA debt restructuring, and ongoing PREPA adjustment plan (5th amendment March 2025). Trend is stable but high uncertainty remains regarding PREPA restructuring and electricity rate increases. Moderate weight as LMM is a minority part of the portfolio.

risks.title: Middle East geopolitical escalation (Iran, Israel, USA)
risks.score_rationale: Major emerging risk described in detail (Hamas attack Oct 7, 2023; US-Israel strikes Feb 28, 2026; Iranian retaliation April 2026). Highly alarming language (« highly unpredictable », « material adverse effect », « sustained volatility »). Clear upward trend with ongoing escalation. Impact on energy markets, trade routes, and travel demand.

risks.title: Dependence on passenger revenue (41-46% of total)
risks.score_rationale: Core business risk: 41.3% of 2025 revenue came from passenger charges (vs 46.1% in 2024). Clear language on structural dependence. Trend is stable but high vulnerability to any shock affecting traffic (economic, health, security). Very high weight for an airport operator.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or related technologies in the report. The company does not appear to position AI as a strategic lever.
